label: Bible Study
prompt: Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an _____ spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
verse: Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
note: Daniel's excellence made the other officials jealous — and that's how the lions' den came about.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For thou art my _____, O LORD: and the LORD will lighten my darkness.
verse: For thou art my lamp, O LORD: and the LORD will lighten my darkness.
note: From David's song after deliverance from Saul: God is his lamp, lighting up the dark.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained _____ in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
verse: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
note: Esther asked for nothing beyond what the chamberlain advised — and won favour with everyone who saw her.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Ephraim is joined to _____: let him alone.
verse: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.
note: God's grim verdict on Ephraim's idolatry: leave him alone.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And he shall be thy _____ unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
verse: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
note: God's compromise for a reluctant Moses: Aaron would be his 'spokesman' — the only time the KJV uses the word.
